body:
Run the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:8791 as a Windows tray app, following synthet-agent-mailbox (tray/AgentMailTray.cs, compiled by the .NET Framework csc.exe, so no extra dependencies) and ai-quotas.

The tray has no console or main window. It declares DPI awareness before any UI: both sibling apps had a blurry icon and menu at 200% scaling without it. Only one instance runs; starting it again opens the dashboard. Left click opens the dashboard, and the menu has Open dashboard and Quit. It starts node bin/agent-flow.js serve hidden, unless a dashboard already answers on 8791, in which case it leaves that one alone and Quit stops only the tray. Quit closes the child's stdin, and serve gets an --exit-on-stdin-close flag so it shuts down cleanly. The log goes to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Agent Flow.

run.cmd installs what is missing, builds, restarts the tray and exits. A script points the existing Agent Flow desktop shortcut at the exe with --open. Autostart only happens with an explicit switch.

body:
Add Jev (TypeSafe System One, via the jev-mcp stdio server) as an automatic review aid, following the swarm review pattern in src/integrations/swarm.ts. Owner decisions (2026-11-07): advise only, never approve or reject; run on demand, plus an opt-in config flag to run on every submit.

Jev judges text, not code. acceptance.text: WHEN the ready queue is empty THEN the context (session-start hook and `flow_context`) tells the agent not to pick work on its own, and to file the user's request as a ticket (`agent-flow create … --ready`, or `flow-plan` for a feature) before claiming it. The MCP overview, the `flow-next` skill and the framework provider doc say the same.

WHEN an agent in a tracked repo makes a real commit (HEAD moved) or runs `gh pr create` while holding no claimed ticket THEN the post-tool hook adds a one-time reminder to create or claim a ticket and reference it in the PR. The hook never denies or allows.
WHEN the nudge already fired in a session, or `hooks.untrackedNudge` is `false`, THEN the post-tool hook stays silent.

WHEN `agent-flow adoption --root <dir> --since <window>` runs THEN it lists every child repo with a tracker, with tickets created, claimed and done in the window plus the commit count, and flags repos that have commits but no tickets. It is read-only and supports `--json`.

WHEN the framework SDD commands run in a repo with `.agent-flow/config.json` THEN they route to agent-flow: `/spec` and `/plan` size the work, `/tasks` imports the table, `/implement` claims a ticket and branches from it, `/test-and-fix` records acceptance-criteria evidence, and `/pr-ready` writes a handoff and submits.
WHEN the work is done THEN the 4 legacy `.agent/backlog/items.md` files with no open items are gone, and each `flow-*` skill exists once per harness for Claude Code (from the plugin).

Actor identity is self-declared everywhere, so gates stop accidents rather than a determined agent. Banning other actors in the MCP server alone would not close the CLI, and could break plugin users because hooks use an 8-character session id while resolveActor uses 12.
